2026-05-29_091935.webp.description: Motorists and cyclists on the Jinsha River (upper Yangtze) Bridge, officially entering Tibet.

2026-05-29_183106.webp.description: On top of Zongla Mountain. This was one of the toughest days of the entire trip, with a 1700m climb over 105km.

2026-05-30_170109.webp.description: The Nu River Bridge. Nu literally means 'angry', reflecting its turbulent nature.

2026-06-01_090531.webp.description: Lower Rawu Lake. This is known as the most scenic ride of the G318 route.

2026-06-01_094903.webp.description: The snow peaks look surprisingly low and close.

2026-06-01_102039.webp.description: One of the best things about a bicycle is that you can stop anywhere without obstructing traffic.

2026-06-01_113246.webp.description: Midui Glacier in the distance. The yellowish glacier-fed stream is merging with the turquoise Parlung Tsangpo River.

2026-06-03_075617.webp.description: Beginning the ride in yet more rain.

2026-06-03_090556.webp.description: Tongmai was once one of the most dangerous stretches of the G318, where rain made landslides frequent. Modern bridges and tunnels have since made it much safer.

2026-06-04_110000.webp.description: Coldest ride of the trip. Got soaked on the climb to Sejila Mountain Pass, 4728m above sea level.

2026-06-05_105843.webp.description: Me at the Nyang River, known as the mother river of Nyingchi.

2026-06-07_094939.webp.description: Last climb to Mila Mountain Pass. At this exact point I had to stop due to a sharp chest pain. Looking back, my cardiopulmonary system had been severely overloaded over the past week, and I should have taken one or two rest days.

2026-06-07_111658.webp.description: 5013m above sea level - the highest point I have ever reached on a bicycle.

2026-06-07_162344.webp.description: A statue of Songtsen Gampo, the seventh-century ruler who unified Tibet.

2026-06-08_170227.webp.description: The Jokhang Temple, the spiritual centre of Tibet for more than 1300 years and the finish point of the G318 pilgrimage. It was built in the seventh century under the reign of Songtsen Gampo. Its most sacred treasure is the Jowo Shakyamuni statue, said to have been made during the lifetime of Shakyamuni Buddha, depicting him at the age of twelve, and brought to Tibet by Princess Wencheng of the Tang Dynasty.

2026-06-09_123357.webp.description: The Potala Palace, whose White Palace historically served as the Dalai Lama's residence and the administrative centre of the Tibetan government. Inside the Red Palace, the reliquary stupa of the Fifth Dalai Lama is adorned with approximately 3.7 tonnes of gold and thousands of precious stones.

2026-06-10_094249.webp.description: Nagenla Pass. My cycling was over, and I was fully enjoying the bus rides.

2026-06-10_130902.webp.description: Namtso, meaning 'Heavenly Lake' in Tibetan, is one of Tibet's most sacred and spectacular alpine lakes.

2026-06-10_140543.webp.description: Nyenchen Tanglha Mountains along the southern shores of Namtso.

2026-06-10_141717.webp.description: Khata scarves on mani stone piles along the shores of Namtso.

2026-06-11_160614.webp.description: Yamdrok Lake, meaning 'Turquoise Lake' in Tibetan, is another of Tibet's three great sacred lakes.

2026-06-11_171144.webp.description: Yamdrok Lake. The railings are fully covered with khata scarves.

2026-06-11_185419.webp.description: Rituo Monastery, a small Tibetan Buddhist monastery perched on a secluded peninsula stretching into the turquoise waters of Yamdrok Lake, often described as one of the loneliest monasteries in the world.

2026-06-11_192646.webp.description: A wild fox near Rituo Monastery.
